6200.full: φαντάζω (φαίνω) [in LXX: Wis.6:16, Sir.31:5 (34:5)* ;] to make visible. In cl. used in pass. only, = φαίνομαι, to become visible, appear: ptcp., Heb.12:21.† (AS)

6201.full: 1. a sparing , νεκύων (Iliad by Homer) 2. absolute thrift, parsimony , (Odyssey by Homer): thrift in exposing oneself to danger, (Thucydides) (ML)

6203.full: 1. the sound of the voice, a voice , (Pindar), etc.: of a person, ὦ φθέγμ᾽ ἀναιδές, for ὦ φθεγξάμενε ἀναιδῆ, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. language, speech , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a saying, word , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. of other sounds, as of birds, cries , (Sophocles Tragicus); of a bull, roaring , (Euripides); φθ. θυείας the grinding of the mortar, (Aristophanes Comicus); of the nightingale's song, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6204.full: φθόγγος, -ου, ὁ (φθέγγομαι), [in LXX: Psa.19:4 (קַו), Wis.19:18 * ;] a sound: Rom.10:18 (LXX) 1Co.14:7.† (AS)

6208.full: φιλόστοργος, -ον (στοργή, family affection), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:13 * ;] tenderly loving, affectionate (Xen., Plut., al.): of Christians, Rom.12:10.† (AS)

6209.full: to be heated, inflamed, to fester , φλεγμαίνουσα πόλις, opposite to ὑγιής, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6213.full: φρυάσσω (so Ps, l.with, NT; elsewhere depon., φρυάσσομαι, Att.. -ττ-), [in LXX: Psa.2:1 (רָגַשׁ), 2Ma.7:34 R, 3Ma.2:2 * ;] prop., of horses, to neigh, whinny and prance (Plut., al.). Metaphorical, to be wanton, insolent: Act.4:25 (LXX).† (AS)

6214.lxx: in LXX: Job.38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Hos.2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pro.21:13 (אָטַם), etc.
6214.full: φράσσω [in LXX: Job.38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Hos.2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pro.21:13 (אָטַם), etc. ;] to fence in, stop, close: στόματα λεόντων, Heb.11:33; στόμα, metaphorically, Rom.3:19; pass., καύχησις, 2Co.11:10.† (AS)

6215.full: 1. a shuddering, shivering , (Plato Philosophus) 2. shuddering , especially from religious awe, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6216.full: φρόνημα, -τος, τό (φρονέω), [in LXX: 2Ma.7:21 2Mac 13:9 * ;] that which is in the mind (the content of φρονεῖν, ICC, Ro., 88), the thought: Rom.8:6-7, 27.† (AS)

6217.full: 1. to roast or fry , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρετμοῖσι φρύξουσι they shall cook with the [wood of] the oars, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., πεφρυγμέναι κριθαί roasted barley, (Thucydides) 2. of the sun, to parch , Lat. torrere, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

6219.full: an instrument for blowing, blowpipe or tube , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6220.full: 1. transitive to puff or blow up, distend , (Aristophanes Comicus); of bag-pipers, (Aristophanes Comicus); φ. τὰς γνάθους to puff them out , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be inflated , ἡ γαστὴρ ἐπεφύσητό μοι (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. metaphorically to puff one up, make him vain , and so to cheat , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be puffed up , ἐπί τινι at a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to blow up, kindle a fire: but also 4. to blow out, extinguish , τὴν λαμπάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. to blow out, spurt out , (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. to blow a wind-instrument, (Euripides) (ML)

6221.full: φωτεινός (WH, φωτινός), ή, όν (φῶς), [in LXX: Sir.17:31 23:19 * ;] bright, light: νεφέλη, Mat.17:5; opposite to σκοτεινός, Mat.6:22, Luk.11:34, 36.† (AS)

6222.full: φίλημα, -τος, τό (φιλέω), [in LXX: Pro.27:6, Sng.1:2 (נְשִׁיקָה) * ;] a kiss: Luk.7:45 22:48; as a token of Christian brotherhood, φ. ἅγιον, Rom.16:16, 1Co.16:20, 2Co.13:12, 1Th.5:26; φ. ἀγάπης, 1Pe.5:14 (see Lft., Notes, 90; DB, DCA, see word "Kiss").† (AS)

6228.full: the chameleon , a kind of lizard known for changing its colour, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

6229.full: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

6230.full: χαρίζομαι (χάρις), [in LXX: Est.8:7 (נָתַן), Sng.1:4 א, Sir.12:3, 2 -4Ma.9:1-32 * ;] __1. to show favour or kindness: with dative of person(s), Gal.3:18. __2. to give freely, bestow: with accusative and dative, Luk.7:21, Act.3:14 25:11, 16 27:24, Rom.8:32, 1Co.2:12, Php.1:29 2:9, Phm 22. __3. In late Gk. (= Lat. condonare), to grant forgiveness, forgive freely: of debt, Luk.7:42-43 (EGT, in l); of sin, 2Co.2:7 2:10 12:13, Eph.4:32, Col.2:13 3:13 (cf. DB, ii, 57a).† (AS)

6231.full: χειρόγραφος, -ον (χείρ, γράφω), [in LXX: Tob.5:3 9:2, 5 * ;] written with the hand. As subst., τὸ χ., a handwriting (Inscr., Polyb., al.): metaphorically, Col.2:14.† (AS)

6232.full: on or of dry land , ὄρνιθες χ. land- birds, opposite to λιμναῖοι, (Herdotus Historicus); χ. κροκόδειλος a lizard, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of landsmen , as opposite to seamen, (Euripides); κῦμα χερσαῖον στρατοῦ, an army, opposite to a fleet, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

6233.full: 1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides) 2. in plural, of the talons of a bird, [variant datesTragica Adespota; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido, (Thucydides) 4. the spur of a mountain or ridge of rocks answering a like purpose, (Thucydides) 5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—; compare χηλεύω. (ML)

6234.full: 1. the office or post of χιλίαρχος, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. the office of the tribuni militares , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6237.full: 1. gut-string, the string of a lyre, Lat. chorda, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. tripe , (Batrachomyomachia): also = χόρδευμα, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6238.full: χρεοφειλέτης (Rec. χρεω-, WH, χρεοφιλ-; see WH, App., 152, 154), -ου, ὁ, (χρέος, a debt, + ὀφειλέτης) [in LXX: Job.31:37, Pro.29:13 * ;] a debtor: Luk.7:41 16:5.† (AS)

6239.full: to be useful or serviceable , τινί to one, (Lucian) (ML)

6241.full: χρή impers. (χράω, see LS, see word), it is necessary: Jas.3:10 (cf. δεῖ.).† (AS)

6242.full: 1. poured, shed , αἷμα χυτόν blood shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of dry things, shot out, heaped up , χυτὴ γαῖα a mound of earth, a sepulchral mound, (Homer):—;as Substantive, χυτός, οῦ, = χῶμα, a mound, bank, dike , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. melted , ἀρτήματα λίθινα χυτά pendants of melted stone, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. generally, liquid, flowing , [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

6243.full: 1. a small stone, pebble , in plural, (Lucian), etc. 2. as collect. in singular, gravel, rubble , used in building, (Thucydides); so also in plural, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6244.full: 1. chaos , the first stateof the universe, (Hesiod), etc. 2. infinite space, the expanse , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. the nether abyss, infinite darkness , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

6246.full: to falter in speech, speak inarticulately :—;so in Mid., (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6248.full: 1. to make an inarticulate noise, to sound, make a noise , (Euripides); ψοφεῖ λάλον τι sounds chatter-like , as if it were tested like a pot, to see if it were cracked, (Aristophanes Comicus); ὥσπερ κύμβαλον ψοφεῖ (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with accusative, ψοφεῖν τὰς θύρας to knock at the door inside, to shew that some one was coming out, Menand.:—;also of the door (intransitive), εἰ αἱ θύραι νύκτωρ ψοφοῖεν, i. e. if they were heard to open , (Lysias Orator) (ML)

6249.full: a wine-cooler , a vessel holding from 2 to 6 μετρηταί, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6251.full: 1. whispering: slanderous , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. as Substantive, ψίθυρος, = ψιθυριστής, a whisperer, slanderer , (Pindar) 3. twittering , of birds, [variant datesAnthology Palantina Perh. formed from the sound. (ML)

6256.full: ἀγγέλλω (ἄγγελος), [in LXX for נגד hi. ;] to announce, report: Jhn.4:51 (WHR omit), 20:18 (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

6259.full: adamantine , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.: —;metaphorically hard as adamant , σιδηροῖς καὶ ἀδαμαντίνοις λόγοις (Plato Philosophus); οὐκ ἀδ. ἐντί, of a girl, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;adverb -νως, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6261.full: 1. want of strength or power, inability, incapacity , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; with genitive, ἀδ. τοῦ ἀδικεῖν for wrong-doing, (Plato Philosophus) 2. poverty , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

6262.full: ἀ-δόκιμος, -ον, [in LXX: Pro.25:4, Isa.1:22 (סִיג) * ;] __1. of things (prop. of metals: LXX, ll. with), not standing the test, rejected: γῆ, Heb.6:8. __2. Of persons, rejected after testing, reprobate: Rom.1:28, 1Co.9:27, 2Co.13:5-7, 2Ti.3:8, Tit.1:16 (Cremer, 212). † (AS)

6266.full: ἀκαταστασία, -ας, ἡ (ἀκατάστατος), [in LXX: Pro.26:28 (מִדְחֶה), Tob.4:13 * ;] instability (MM, VGT, see word); hence, confusion, tumult: 1Co.14:33, Jas.3:16; pl. (Bl., §32, 6), Luk.21:9, 2Co.6:5, 12:20 (Polyb., al.; see Cremer, 739).† (AS)

6267.full: ἀκατάσχετος, -ον (κατέχω), [in LXX: Job.31:11, 3Ma.6:17 * ;] that cannot be restrained: Jas.3:8 Rec. (for -στατος, which see).† (AS)

6271.full: ἀκροατής, οῦ, ὁ (see supr.) [in LXX: Isa.3:3 (לַחַשׁ), Sir.3:29 ;] a hearer: Rom.2:13, Jas.1:22, 23, 25.† (AS)

6272.full: to cut off the extremities, mutilate , τὰς πρῴρας ἠκρωτηρίασαν cut the beaks off the prows, (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., τὰς τριήρεις ἀκρωτηριασάμενοι (Xenophon Historicus); perfect passive in middle sense, ἠκρωτηριασμένοι τὰς πατρίδας having mutilated their countries, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

6274.full: to make false pretensions , of the Sophists, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6276.full: estrangement , τῆς ξυμμαχίας οὐχ ὁμοία ἡ ἀλλ. its estrangement , its loss , (Thucydides) (ML)

6283.full: ἀ-μετάθετος, -ον (μετατίθημι), [in LXX: 3Ma.5:1 3Mac 5:12 * ;] immutable: Heb.6:18; as subat., τὸ ἀ., immutability, Heb.6:17 (see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

6284.full: decree of amnestyetfulness, decree of amnesty

6285.full: an error, fault, offence , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;also, metri grat., ἀπλάκημα, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

s: to squeeze out like milk, to press out
6287.full: 1. to milk sheep and goats; βόας (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —;Mid., in metaphorically sense, ἀμέλγεσθαι τοὺς ξένους to milk them dry, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to draw milk from the animals, ἀμ. γάλα (Herdotus Historicus); Pass., ὄϊες ἀμελγόμεναι γάλα having milk drawn from them, milch- ewes, (Iliad by Homer) 3. metaphorically to squeeze out like milk, to press out , ἐκ βοτρύων ξανθὸν ἄμελξε γάνος [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. to drink , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

6288.full: ἀμέριμνος, -ον (μέριμνα), [in LXX: Wis.6:15 7:23 * ;] free from anxiety or care: Mat.28:14, 1Co.7:32 (for exx., see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

6289.full: to shoot up, grow up again , of Plants, (Plato Philosophus); of a city, (Herdotus Historicus); of misfortunes, to spring up, be rank , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6291.full: ἀνα-δέχομαι [in LXX: 2Ma.6:19 2Mac 8:36 * ;] __1. to assume, undertake (in π. frequently as legal term: MM, VGT, see word): ἐπαγγελίας, Heb.11:17. __2. = cl. ὑποδέχομαι, to receive: of guests, Act.28:7.† (AS)

6292.full: ἀνα-ζώννυμι [in LXX: Jdg.18:16, Pro.31:17 (חָגַר)* ;] to gird up: figuratively, τ. ὀσφύας τ. διανοίας, 1Pe.1:13.† (AS)

6293.full: 1. to drive back , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to beat back an assailant, (Thucydides) 3. to stop:—; Pass. to be stopped, stop short , τινός from a thing, (Lucian) (ML)

s: to come to oneself again, revive
6294.full: 1. to flame up, take fire , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. metaphorically to break out anew , as war, (Plutarch) 3. to come to oneself again, revive , (Plutarch) (ML)

s: to set on the wing, excite vehemently
to be in a state of excitement
6296.full: 1. properly of a bird, to raise its feathers : hence, ἀν. ἐθείρας (Euripides) 2. metaphorically to set on the wing, excite vehemently , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; Pass. to be in a state of excitement , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)

s: to make to break forth, utter
6297.full: 1. to break up the ground, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to break through a wall, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., ἡ ναῦς ἀναρρήγνυται τὴν παρεξειρεσίαν the ship has its bow broken through , (Thucydides) 3. to tear open a carcase, of lions, (Iliad by Homer); of Ajax, δίχα ἀνερρήγνυ was cleaving them asunder, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to make to break forth, utter , like Lat. rumpere voces, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀν. πόλιν to make it break out, excite greatly , (Plutarch):—;Pass. to burst forth ; metaphorically of persons, ἀναρρήγνυσθαι πρὸς ὀργήν (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 5. intransitive to break forth , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

6298.full: ἀνα-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀναστρέφομαι) [in LXX: Tob.4:14, 2Ma.5:8 2Mac 6:23 * ;] __1. a turning down or back, a wheeling about (Soph., Thuc., al.). __2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; see: ἀναστρέφω, and cf. Hort on Jas.3:13; MM, VGT, see word), manner of life, behaviour, conduct: Gal.1:13, Eph.4:22, 1Ti.4:12, Heb.13:7, Jas.3:13, 1Pe.1:15 1:18 2:12 3:1-2 3:16, 2Pe.2:7 3:11.† (AS)
